Text attachments in a BB chat now reach Muse: `promptText` reads `resource_link` `file://` files and inlines UTF-8 text under the file name in a `~~~` fence. Binary files get a “not sent” line; a file over 200 000 characters is cut with the truncation note. `extractBbContext` still joins only text blocks.

Changed paths:
- `bridge/acp-prompt.mjs`
- `tests/acp-attachments.test.mjs`
- `package.json`
- `package-lock.json`
- `version.ts`

Checked: `node /tmp/muse-attach/check.mjs "$PWD"` printed `OK`. `node --test tests/acp-attachments.test.mjs tests/version.test.mjs` — 8 pass, 0 fail.

```plan-fact
[
  {"item":1,"status":"done","evidence":["bridge/acp-prompt.mjs:90-104","bridge/acp-prompt.mjs:116-146","cmd:node /tmp/muse-attach/check.mjs \"$PWD\""]},

  {"item":3,"status":"done","evidence":["package.json:3","package-lock.json:3","package-lock.json:9","version.ts:3","cmd:node --test tests/acp-attachments.test.mjs tests/version.test.mjs"]}

```

APPROACH: Leave `extractBbContext` on the text-only join; give `promptText` a second join that inlines `file://` attachments in order, with tilde fences so markdown in the file stays intact.
LESSON: BB attachments live outside the workspace as `resource_link` blocks, so Muse `read_file` cannot see them — the agent has to put the file text into the message.

dispatchContext.rulesText:
- In verification scripts and tests that create temp dirs, use /tmp explicitly (mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX, or TMPDIR=/tmp): the writer sandbox denies mkdtemp in the system TMPDIR under /var/folders. Keep PM-written check scripts in /tmp/<name>/ (the guard blocks .mjs under .agents/).
- In a folder without git (live-folder mode), never put a task's expected_outputs or owns_paths under .bb/ (chat folders): the live snapshot skips .bb, so a file written there is never counted as produced and the task blocks as missing expected_outputs. Put task deliverables in a project folder such as docs/ or reports/.
- Правя тестовый файл из owns_paths, меняй только ожидаемые значения внутри существующих строгих assert (deepEqual/equal) и добавляй новые проверки рядом — не удаляй строки assert и не ослабляй строгую проверку до assert.ok/includes/truthiness; перед ответом перечитай свой diff по тестам и верни всё, что стало слабее: test_fit помечает это как сломанную проверку, и попытки сгорают до лимита.
- For a BB ACP provider, check every launch spec and output shape against BB's own bridge code before shipping: permission flags are inserted at permissionCli.insertAfterArgs (default 0, so a /bin/sh -c wrapper needs insertAfterArgs after its args), and agent_message_chunk keeps only text (image blocks are dropped; show pictures as Markdown ![alt](workspace-relative path)).

In bridge/acp-tools.mjs, tool call detection currently relies on TOOL_BLOCK_RE (/```muse-tool[ \\t]*\\r?\\n?([\\s\\S]*?)```/g), which strictly requires a closing ```. When Muse truncates the closing fence, parseToolCall returns { kind: \"none\", text }, causing the tool call to be missed and eventually forcing the truncated text to be treated as a final answer after MAX_BLOCKLESS_REPLIES. Real session data from Muse chat 84a16a39 revealed that 10 of ~40 tool replies across two chats exhibited this truncation on the server side.\n\nThe plan (.agents/plans/muse-unclosed-tool-block.md) specifies updating parseToolCall to: (1) retain precedence for the last valid closed block; (2) if no closed block matches or if a closed match fails parsing due to backticks inside a string, fall back to an unclosed block scanner; (3) scan from the last unclosed ```muse-tool opener tracking string escapes and nesting depth, completing valid JSON at depth 0 with remaining text added to thought; (4) append missing closing brackets/braces ('}', ']') in stack order if scanning ends outside a string with depth > 0; and (5) return an error object if scanning cuts off inside an open string.
